note: Golden question set for the retrieval/extraction suite. Ground truth is known because the corpus is synthetic — no real filing was used, so there is no licensing or PII exposure, and no chance a model has memorized the answer from pre-training. That last point matters more than it looks: on a real 10-K a model can answer from memory without reading the context, which would make a retrieval benchmark measure recall of training data instead of retrieval quality.

questions.question: What was Northwind's consolidated revenue in fiscal 2024?
questions.why: Baseline lookup. Any pipeline that fails this is broken, not merely weak.

questions.question: What was Northwind's consolidated revenue in fiscal 2023?
questions.why: The figure appears in BOTH annual reports — as the current year in the 2023 10-K and as the comparative in the 2024 10-K. Either citation is correct. The trap is answering 4,182.6 because the retriever surfaced the wrong year's section.

questions.question: What percentage of cost of revenue did diesel represent in fiscal 2023?
questions.why: Near-identical sentences in the two filings differing only in year and figure (14.6% vs 16.1%). This is the case that motivates lexical over embedding retrieval — semantically the two sentences are the same sentence.

questions.question: What was Cold Chain segment operating margin in fiscal 2024 according to the segment detail table?
questions.why: Tests CSV ingestion. A chunker that splits rows from the header cannot answer this, and a raw CSV dump gives the model an unlabeled column.

questions.question: The 10-K narrative and the segment table both give Cold Chain operating margin for fiscal 2024. Do they agree?
questions.why: They do not: the table says 14.5% and the Q3 call says 14.9% for the quarter, while 201.4/1388.9 computes to 14.5% for the year. A pipeline should surface both figures with their periods rather than silently picking one. NOT CURRENTLY SCORED AS SUCH (noted 2026-08-13): expectConflict is parsed by the suite schema and read by no scorer. On retrieval this row is scored on nothing at all, and end to end scoreAnswer only requires that SOME grounded fact came back — a single unrelated revenue figure marks it correct. Implementing both-sources-cited scoring is open work; until then treat this row as measuring nothing.

questions.question: Northwind's credit agreement restricts share repurchases above a leverage threshold. Was the company inside that threshold at December 31, 2024?
questions.why: Two documents, no shared vocabulary: the covenant says 'Restricted Payments' and '3.25 to 1.00', the 10-K says 'repurchased 4.1 million shares' and '2.6x'. The answer (yes, 2.6x is inside 3.25x) requires both. This is the question that separates single-shot retrieval from multi-hop.

questions.question: How much borrowing capacity did Northwind have available at the end of fiscal 2024?
questions.why: DELIBERATELY INCLUDED AS A KNOWN WEAKNESS. The corpus never says 'borrowing capacity'; it says 'undrawn capacity under its Revolving Credit Facility'. Lexical retrieval is expected to underperform here, and the suite reports that rather than omitting the case. If a semantic retriever is ever added, this is the question it must win.

questions.question: What was Northwind's revenue in fiscal 2025?
questions.why: The corpus ends at fiscal 2024 and contains a 2025 GUIDANCE range (4,150 to 4,200) that is not an actual. The correct answer is an empty extraction. This is the single most important row in the set: a pipeline that cannot decline will report guidance as actuals, and that failure is invisible on every other question.

questions.question: What was Northwind's customer churn rate in fiscal 2024?
questions.why: Nothing in the corpus discusses churn. Retrieval will still return the customer-concentration section because it matches on 'customer', so this measures whether the model declines when handed plausible-but-irrelevant context — the dominant real failure mode of RAG.

questions.question: What was Northwind's free cash flow in fiscal 2024?
questions.why: Stated explicitly (283.4) AND derivable (596.2 - 312.8). Both are acceptable, but the extraction gate requires the value to appear in the quote, so a model that computes rather than quotes is rejected — by design. Tests that the groundedness rule bites on a case where the arithmetic is right.

questions.question: Northwind's Q3 2024 net leverage was 2.7x. What is the maximum leverage its credit agreement permits, and how much headroom is that?

questions.question: What full-year fiscal 2024 Adjusted EBITDA guidance range did Northwind give on its Q3 2024 earnings call?
questions.why: Transcripts have no markdown headings — only ALL-CAPS speaker lines. Tests the heading heuristic on unstructured plain text; a failure here shows up as the whole 12k-token transcript arriving as one chunk.
